# Savi Saluwadana

> Savi Saluwadana is a software and product engineer based in Sri Lanka with a strong interest in software architecture, systems design, Platform Engineering, DevOps and AI-enabled systems. His work spans customer-facing products, Go backends, Kubernetes, developer platforms, CI/CD, operational automation, multi-tenant systems, MCP integrations and production-minded software design.

## Product work

### Avara Real Estate
Repository: https://github.com/RealEstateSassApplication/AvaraRealEstate

A Sri Lankan property platform for rentals, property sales and short-term bookings. It includes advanced and geospatial search, role-based users, property management, availability and booking workflows, PayHere payments, S3 media storage and admin operations.

### Blu.lk
Website: https://blu.lk/

A Sri Lankan home-services platform connecting customers with skilled professionals. The product includes service discovery, booking flows, provider and worker operations, payments, scheduling and service fulfillment across home-service categories.

### FreshPick / FreshOnTime
Website: https://freshpick.lk/

A premium food-commerce and recurring-delivery platform for Colombo, combining fresh groceries, local products, prepared meals, repeat purchasing, recurring delivery and business ordering into one customer experience.

### TimelyHelp.lk
Website: https://timelyhelp.lk/
Repository: private

A mental-healthcare product for practitioner discovery, secure consultation booking and digital care journeys. Savi worked on the product and frontend experience. The current frontend uses Next.js 15 and TypeScript with NextAuth, practitioner APIs, Zoom Video SDK, Sentry monitoring, internationalization and protected user flows across discovery, checkout, dashboards and consultation surfaces.

## Engineering systems and developer tooling

### DevRelOS
Repository: https://github.com/savisaluwadana/DevRelOS

A developer-intelligence operating system for signal discovery, community and content workflows, developer feedback, campaigns, media workflows and measurable outcomes. The self-hosted architecture uses a Next.js operator dashboard, Go API and workers, PostgreSQL and an authenticated MCP server.

### Property Management OS
Repository: https://github.com/RealEstateSassApplication/property-management-OS

A multi-tenant rental operations platform covering properties, units, owners, tenants, leases, rent, maintenance, documents, notifications and controlled agent-assisted operations. The system uses Next.js, Go, PostgreSQL, OIDC/JWT, organization-scoped RBAC, S3-compatible storage, transactional outbox delivery, OpenAPI and MCP.

### RapidReach
Repository: https://github.com/savisaluwadana/RapidReachBloWebsite

A developer publication and developer-tool discovery product built with Next.js, TypeScript, MongoDB and Vercel Blob. It includes editorial workflows, comments, likes, search, tool profiles, media uploads and structured discovery surfaces for search engines and agents.

## Software architecture
Savi is especially interested in software architecture and systems design: defining clear domain boundaries, service responsibilities, data ownership, API contracts, background workflows and operational boundaries that let systems evolve without making every change expensive or difficult to reason about.

## Platform Engineering and DevOps
Savi works across the path from source code to reliable production: developer platforms, self-service workflows, Kubernetes, containers, CI/CD, release automation, observability, reliability, debugging and operational safety. The goal is to reduce developer friction without hiding the underlying system so completely that it becomes difficult to understand or operate.

He is particularly interested in software problems involving marketplaces, payments, workflow automation, operational platforms, data-heavy systems, logistics, scheduling, asset management, infrastructure and software that interacts with real-world operations.

## Engineering principles
- Treat the product as a complete system: interface, domain logic, data, payments, infrastructure and operations.
- Use architecture to make ownership, state and change easier to reason about.
- Keep domain rules authoritative on the server.
- Prefer one clear system of record before adding parallel state systems.
- Treat agents as authenticated clients, not privileged back doors.
- Make automation observable and externally consequential actions inspectable.
- Build paved roads that reduce friction while preserving debuggability.
- Add distributed infrastructure when the workload requires it, not for appearance.
